task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Supreme Court seeks UP Police response to plea over attack on lawyers in Ghaziabad society
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought responses from the Uttar Pradesh Police on a petition alleging failure to register a case of attempted murder after a group of unidentified men assaulted several advocates, including a woman lawyer, during a dispute over alleged illegal construction in Ghaziabad. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana issued notice on a petition filed by the advocates. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The petitioners include Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) members A Deepa and A Deb Kumar. Delhi High Court advocates Vipin Sharma and Anup Goyal are also petitioners in the matter. All of them reside at 'Apex The Florus' society in Vasundhara, Ghaziabad. According to the petition, the incident took place on the night of October 22 when two residents brought a group of unidentified men into the residential complex following a dispute over illegal construction and blockage of passage. items.title: Jet Airways liquidator moves NCLAT for $92.13 million refund from Boeing over undelivered aircraft
items.summary: Jet Airways’ liquidator has moved the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) seeking a refund of $92.13 million paid to Boeing as advances for aircraft that were never delivered [Jet Airways Vs Boeing]. A bench of Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan and Technical Member Naresh Salecha issued notice to Boeing after observing that the appeal required consideration. Boeing’s counsel accepted notice and was granted two weeks to file a reply. The liquidator was given one week thereafter to file a rejoinder. The matter will be heard next in the first week of December. The appeal challenged a September 11 order of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) dismissing liquidator Satish Kumar Gupta’s application seeking recovery of $92,129,387 from Boeing. During the hearing at NCLAT today, the counsel for the liquidator submitted that Boeing had forfeited Jet Airways’ advance payments and then lodged a claim for the unpaid balance during the airline’s corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP). The counsel clarified that the appeal concerned recovery of the advances. The liquidator sought notice without pressing for interim relief. The dispute arose from two purchase agreements exec

items.title: Delhi High Court suspends its order for criminal complaint against 6 CBI officials over false statements
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has put in abeyance its order directing initiation of criminal proceedings against six former and serving Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officers [Ashok Kumar Aggarwal v. Sushil Dewan & Ors] . On October 6, Justice Madhu Jain had ordered action against the CBI officials for allegedly making false statements before a court about correspondence with the government while challenging the discharge of a former Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer in a case. The Court had allowed IRS officer Ashok Kumar Aggarwal's plea and directed the Special Judge (CBI) to file a written complaint against Sushil Dewan, Vineet Vinayak, Amit Kumar, Raman Tyagi, Prem Kumar Gautam and Md Azad. However, in an order passed on November 3, Justice Mini Pushkarna said that the direction will remain in abeyance. The matter will be heard next on February 4, 2027. Justice Mini Pushkarna The Court passed the order after two former CBI officers - Sushil Dewan and Raman Tyagi - filed applications seeking recall of the order. The applicants, supported by the CBI, argued that the judgment was passed without hearing them. Only Dewan was a party to the appeal. He claimed he was served on a wro

items.title: Purchasable FAR destroying Gurugram, Noida: P&H High Court moots stay in Haryana
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Wednesday warned that it will stop implementation of the purchasable Floor Area Ratio (FAR) for constructions in Haryana, observing that it was leading to destruction of urban landscape in cities like Gurugram and Noida. Purchasable FAR is the extra floor area that a developer or property owner in Haryana can build by paying an additional fee to the government, over and above the normal FAR permitted under building regulations. A bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Rohit Kapoor said purchasable FAR destroys the purpose of having a building code. "We have very strong reservations with this purchasable concept. This entire purchasable concept is nothing but a way of distorting and destroying entire building code," the bench stated. The Court said Chandigarh has remained a liveable city only because it does not have the concept of purchasable FIR. It added that cities like Gurgaon and Noida are being destroyed because of purchasable FAR. "What is not permitted otherwise under the building bye-laws is being allowed in the form of one policy or other," the bench said. items.title: Delhi government lawyer grants consent for contempt of court case against CJP's Ratna Singh
items.summary: Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel (ASC) Amol Sinha has granted consent to initiate criminal contempt of court proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) legal head Ratna Singh over her social media criticism of a Chief Judicial Magistrate in Saket Courts. Advocate Kausik Chatterjee had sought action against Singh through a representation dated October 14 and a supplementary one dated October 28. In his November 2 response to Chatterjee, Sinha said the posts prima facie attract Section 2(c)(i) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971. The controversy arose from proceedings before Chief Judicial Magistrate Abhinav Pandey of South-East District. Singh had approached the Court seeking an FIR against police personnel who detained her on October 10 while she was trying to join CJP protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. She had also sought release from alleged detention. The Court declined the relief. Singh then posted the following on X: "Judge serving the master. items.title: Supreme Court seeks response from Allahabad HC on plea to remove POCSO judge facing rape case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Allahabad High Court administration and Additional District Judge (ADJ) Ashok Bhartendu on a petition filed by a rape survivor seeking Bhartendu's removal as a special POCSO judge in view of a pending rape case against him in Delhi. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana also said that it would examine the progress of the vigilance complaint lodged against Bhartendu. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana During the hearing, advocate Rakesh Kumar Singh, appearing for the rape survivor, highlighted the irony of a judicial officer presiding over a court designated under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) while facing criminal proceedings for rape himself. "Higher judicial officer is unfortunately an accused and cognisance has already been taken, and still he is continuing as a POCSO judge... His quashing petition is pending, but there is no stay," Singh submitted. items.title: Delhi High Court quashes CIC order directing HC to provide data under RTI on delayed judgments
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has set aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing the court’s Public Information Officer (PIO) to locate and provide details of cases in which judgments were reserved but pronounced more than two months later [Public Information Officer v PD Gupta] . Justice Amit Mahajan allowed a 2011 petition filed by the PIO of the High Court against the CIC’s May 26, 2011, order. The Court observed that while timely delivery of judgments is a matter of public concern, the consideration of public interest arises only when the information exists. “The same cannot be used to compel a public authority to create information which is not held by it,” the Court said. In the present case such information was not maintained by the High Court, and in order to provide the information sought, the public authority would have to examine records of all cases heard by a particular judge and prepare a fresh compilation, the Court noted. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The case arose from a Right to Information (RTI) application filed in 2009 by former judicial officer PD Gupta. items.title: Our dignity is at stake: Supreme Court directs Centre to bring back child taken from its custody to Russia
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Central government to take urgent steps to bring a child back to India after he was taken to Russia by his Russian mother despite the child having been placed in the Court's custody earlier [ Viktoriia Basu v. State of West Bengal ]. In an order passed on November 3, a Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu took serious exception to the conduct of the child's mother, Russian national Viktoriia Basu, who allegedly left India through Nepal with her young son and travelled to Russia. The Bench said that the Court's dignity was at stake and that the mother could not be allowed to take advantage of the leniency shown to her during the proceedings. “We are not going to leave this. Our dignity is at stake. After we had taken the child into our custody, the mother, with the help of the Russian Embassy, went away through Nepal. We feel the Russian Federation is aware of it. You (Centre) have to throw all your weight behind this,” the Court orally remarked. items.title: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity for CEC, Election Commissioners
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Central government and the Election Commission of India (ECI) to a plea challenging a legal provision that protects the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners (EC) from any legal action for any act done in the course of their duties. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on a petition filed by activist and lawyer, Arun Kumar Agrawal. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The plea challenges the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. This provision extends lifelong protection to the CEC and EC from civil or criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of their official duties. The plea points out that similar protection to other constitutional functionaries for actions done in the course of their duties usually extends only to acts done or intended to be done in good faith. items.title: Supreme Court declines to entertain plea challenging Rajasthan Cricket Association elections
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to entertain a challenge concerning the internal election disputes, electoral rolls, and administrative wrangles of the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA), leaving all contested issues to be adjudicated by the Rajasthan High Court [Rajendra Singh vs State of Rajasthan]. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana refused to interfere with the ongoing proceedings, underlining that High Courts are constitutional forums fully equipped to resolve such grievances without apex court oversight. "Let us not predict what the High Court will do. Let us not predict what the outcome will be. If the High Court errs, we are there. But let us not handhold the High Court. The High Court knows how to take a decision and what to do," remarked Justice Bagchi during the hearing. The Court was hearing a petition preferred by Rajendra Singh Nandhu, Secretary of the Nagaur District Cricket Association, challenging the manner in which the RCA's electoral process was conducted. items.title: Supreme Court pulls up Bhupesh Baghel for attempt to delay trial in plea challenging his election
items.summary: The Supreme Court today pulled up former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister and Congress MLA Bhupesh Baghel over attempts to delay the trial of an election petition challenging his 2023 State assembly election victory from the Patan constituency [ Bhupesh Baghel v. Vijay Baghel ]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana proceeded to uphold the Chhattisgarh High Court's dismissal of Baghel's plea to first examine if the election petition filed against him was barred by limitation. The top court also expressed displeasure over the repeated attempts to defer proceedings. "Let the trial proceed. You are delaying as much as possible. You will have a decision," said Justice Mohana. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The dispute stems from the 2023 Chhattisgarh Assembly polls, where Bhupesh Baghel won the Patan seat by securing 95,438 votes against BJP candidate Vijay Baghel’s 75,715 votes. Vijay Baghel filed an election petition alleging that Bhupesh Baghel violated the statutory 48-hour "silence period" under Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by holding a rally/roadshow on November 16, 2023.

items.title: Cannot assume a majority community will vote on community or caste lines: Supreme Court on plea over SC/ST reserved seat
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether keeping assembly constituencies in Uttar Pradesh reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) candidates for decades without rotation would amount to restriction of electoral choice. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition challenging the continued reservation of certain assembly constituencies for SC/ST candidates without rotation for several decades. Justice Bagchi observed that there cannot be an assumption that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. "That proceeds on the idea that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. They may not vote on community and caste lines. The High Court cannot judicially pronounce on a democratic choice. That is for the voters to decide." He added that the right to vote was not affected merely because a particular constituency was reserved for candidates belonging to a particular community. "Your right to vote is not in issue. Your right to vote cannot be taken away. You can vote for any community. But if you say that you cannot vote for your community, that will not be

items.title: Madras High Court grants relief to DMK councillor booked for remarks against CM Vijay
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Monday observed that the police serve the State and not the political party in power, while granting anticipatory bail to a Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) councillor accused of making derogatory remarks against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Vijay [ D Sudha v. State ]. Justice N Ramesh said that an impartial police force was essential to constitutional governance and that the machinery of criminal law could not be deployed merely because political speech offended those holding public office. " An even hand between the ruling party and its opponents is not a courtesy the police extend; it is a condition of their constitutional legitimacy. The police serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes ," the Court observed. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday quashed the criminal defamation case filed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC), Chief Minister DK Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah over the publication of advertisements accusing the previous BJP government of corruption [Siddaramaiah & others v. BJP]. Justice M Nagaprasanna allowed the petitions filed by the Congress leaders seeking quashing of the criminal proceedings. Justice M Nagaprasanna The case was registered against KPCC, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Shivakumar and Siddaramaiah over allegations that they were responsible for publishing newspaper advertisements containing derogatory allegations against the BJP-led State government, which was in power between 2019 and 2023 under former Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai. The advertisements had described the then BJP government as a “40 per cent commission sarkar” , alleging that commissions were being charged in public procurement, allotment of contract works and supply of COVID-19-related materials, among other activities. Justice Tushar Rao Gedela However, the Court was informed that negotiations with 4 PM News have failed so far. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a show cause notice to the Municipal Commissioner, seeking a response as to why contempt action should not be initiated. The Court also dismissed the commissioner's plea for more time to comply, slapping ₹5 lakh costs and ordering a halt to salary payments. Additionally, CJI Kant questioned whether municipal officers were deliberately avoiding compliance with the Supreme Court's directions. "Does it not show that your officers are colluding? We will send him to jail and then he will understand the sanctity of the Supreme Court order. Is he obliging us?" said CJI Kant .
